question: Over the last twenty years, what has happened to the share of the world's people living in extreme poverty?
answer: Almost halved. In Hans Rosling's surveys most people picked one of the other two, doing worse than chimpanzees would by picking at random. Sudden disasters make the news; a slow, steady improvement never does.
move: Bad news is reported; slow improvement isn't. Ask what the trend says before the headline.
trap: 'Almost doubled': it matches every image of poverty you have seen.
simply: If you only ever hear about the houses that burn down, you'd think the whole town is on fire, even while most houses are getting new roofs.
why: What you think the world is like decides what you fear, give to and vote for. Getting the trend right changes all three.
